## Natural history notes

A medium-sized sphinx moth characterized by streamlined brown to olive-gray forewings, orange hindwings, a thick pointed abdomen, and the fast, powerful flight typical of hawk moths. In Florida, it is found in woodlands, hammocks, forest edges, gardens, parks, vineyards, and other areas where Virginia creeper, grape, peppervine, or related host plants occur. Adults are mostly active at dusk and night and may visit flowers or come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on grape-family vines and related plants, often resting along leaf midribs and developing into smooth hornworms with a tail-like horn.
